verdict: Otis grew sales 6%, carried by its high-margin Service business — maintaining and modernizing the elevators it already sold.

segments.name: Service
segments.note: Maintenance, repair and modernization of elevators and escalators — recurring, high-margin work on the huge installed base.

segments.name: New Equipment
segments.note: Selling and installing new elevators and escalators for buildings under construction.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, service management and the back office.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: New elevator technology and digital service tools.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: A small net operating charge that sits above operating profit in Otis's own statement.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $68M, shown below operating profit in Otis's statement (non-service pension cost was zero this quarter).

takeaways.title: Service is the engine — and the profit
takeaways.text: Service sales rose 8% to $2.6B at a 24.2% segment operating margin, versus thin margins on new equipment. Modernization orders rose 10% and its backlog grew 20%.

takeaways.title: GAAP EPS rose 14% — with an asterisk
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS jumped mainly because last year carried UpLift restructuring and separation costs. Adjusted EPS was flat at $1.05, and adjusted operating profit slipped $6M.

takeaways.title: Steady cash, steady returns
takeaways.text: Adjusted free cash flow was $272M in the quarter; year to date Otis has returned about $1.3B to shareholders in buybacks and dividends.

oneTimers: The GAAP comparison is flattered by last year: Q3 2025 included $27M of UpLift restructuring, $10M of UpLift transformation costs and $4M of separation-related costs. On an adjusted basis, operating profit fell $6M year over year.
footerNote: Net income shown ($426M) is before $12M attributable to noncontrolling interests (attributable: $414M).
follow100Note: The $6M other operating expense, net sits above operating profit in Otis's own statement, so it is grouped with operating expenses in the flow.
